A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we demonstrated the existence of a baroreceptor reflex arc in the rat and showed that this reflex arc is located in the brainstem, that it is essential for the regulation of blood pressure, and that it is sensitive to anesthetic agents.
the nucleus tractus is the site for the termination of baroreceptor afferents and is the site where the reflex response to changes in blood pressure is initiated.
the nucleus tractus of the rat is an important site for integration and modulation of the cardiovascular system.

the brainstem plays an important role in the control of blood pressure, and that the brainstem is the most important site for baroreceptor reflex regulation of arterial pressure.
